**Finding submitted — deviation (MFN).**

- **Responsive locations:** § 7.2 (p0026) is the only operative MFN in the document; § 12.3 (p0044) disclaims any most-favoured-customer commitment and directly conflicts with it. No other MFN/right-to-match language exists (searches on "favourable", "most-favoured", "match", "no less favourable" returned nothing further), and there are no cross-references to Section 7.2.
- **Classification:** § 7.2 runs against us — we must disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer before engaging another provider. It is unlimited as to product, unlimited in duration, and has no like-for-like comparison carve-outs, so it fails all three fallback elements and sits in walk-away territory.
- **Cure:** a single surgical replacement of the offending sentence in § 7.2 with a confirmation that we owe no disclosure/matching or most-favoured-customer obligation — aligning § 7.2 with § 12.3 and meeting the preferred element. Vendor-granted MFN in our favour is untouched and remains welcome.
